recipes.title: Brown Butter Apple Crumble
recipes.coverPrompt: Golden oat crumble over bubbling apples in a well-loved enamel dish, potluck table, warm late-afternoon light.
recipes.description: The crumble we bring to every team potluck. Browning the butter first makes the topping taste like toffee.

steps.description: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat and keep swirling until it smells nutty and the solids turn deep golden. Pour into a bowl and let it cool for a few minutes.
Stir the flour, oats, brown sugar and salt into the brown butter until it clumps. Chill while you prepare the fruit.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Peel, core and slice the apples, then toss with the lemon juice, cinnamon and sugar in a baking dish.
Scatter the topping over the apples and bake until the fruit bubbles at the edges and the top is crisp and brown.
Let it settle for ten minutes so the juices thicken, then serve warm with cold cream or vanilla ice cream.

recipes.title: Honeycrisp Galette
recipes.coverPrompt: Rustic free-form galette with fanned Honeycrisp slices and a sugared, flaky edge on parchment, orchard morning light.
recipes.description: A free-form apple tart for people who think pie crust is too fussy. Thin slices, a buttery fold, and a glossy apricot glaze.

steps.description: Rub the cold butter into the flour, sugar and salt until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces. Add the ice water a spoonful at a time until it just holds together. Flatten into a disc, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Core the apples, slice them 3 mm thick, and toss with the sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon.
Roll the pastry into a 30 cm round on a floured sheet of parchment. Fan the apples in overlapping rings, leaving a 5 cm border, then fold the border up over the fruit.
Brush the folded edge with beaten egg and sprinkle with demerara. Bake until the pastry is deep golden and the apples are tender.
Warm the apricot jam with a splash of water and brush it over the hot apples. Cool for 15 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Tarte Tatin
recipes.coverPrompt: Just-flipped tarte Tatin with glossy amber caramelized apples on a cast-iron pan, a little caramel pooling, moody kitchen light.
recipes.description: Apples cooked in amber caramel under a lid of puff pastry, then flipped. The one dessert worth saying "one more thing" for.

steps.description: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). In a 24 cm ovenproof skillet, cook the sugar and water over medium heat without stirring until it turns deep amber. Take it off the heat and stir in the butter.
Peel, halve and core the apples. Stand them tightly on their sides in the caramel, rounded side down. Cook over low heat so the caramel bubbles up around them.
Lay the puff pastry over the pan, tuck the edges down around the apples, and cut a few small vents.
Bake until the pastry is puffed and dark golden.
Rest for 5 minutes. Put a plate over the pan and, using oven gloves, flip it in one confident move. Serve warm with crème fraîche.

recipes.title: Waldorf Salad
recipes.coverPrompt: Crisp Waldorf salad with green and red apple, celery, grapes and toasted walnuts in a white bowl, bright daylight.
recipes.description: Crisp apples, celery, grapes and toasted walnuts in a light lemony dressing. Lunch for the whole design review.

steps.description: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, shaking often, until fragrant. Let them cool, then chop roughly.
Whisk the yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, honey and a pinch of salt.
Dice the apples, slice the celery and halve the grapes. Fold everything into the dressing with the walnuts and serve over the lettuce leaves.

recipes.title: Cider-Braised Pork Chops with Apples
recipes.coverPrompt: Seared pork chops in a skillet with soft cider-braised apple wedges, onions and thyme, glossy pan sauce, cozy evening light.
recipes.description: Golden pork chops braised in hard cider with apples, onion and thyme. One pan, thirty-five minutes.

steps.description: Season the chops well with salt and pepper. Sear in the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until deeply browned on both sides. Move them to a plate.
Lower the heat. Add the butter, onion and apple wedges and cook until they start to caramelise at the edges.
Pour in the cider and mustard, scraping up the browned bits. Add the thyme, return the chops and simmer gently, covered, until the pork is just cooked through.
Lift out the chops to rest. Stir the cream into the pan and bubble until the sauce coats a spoon. Spoon over the chops.

recipes.title: Apple Cider Donuts
recipes.coverPrompt: Stack of cinnamon-sugar apple cider donuts on a wooden board beside a mug of cider, autumn farm-stand feel.
recipes.description: Baked, not fried, with reduced cider in the batter and a crackly cinnamon-sugar coat.

steps.description: Simmer the cider in a saucepan until it has reduced to about 120 ml. Let it cool.

Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a donut pan. Whisk the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt. In another bowl whisk the melted butter, sugar, egg and reduced cider, then fold the two together until just combined.
Pipe the batter into the pan, filling each ring about three-quarters full. Bake until springy.
While still warm, brush each donut with melted butter and roll in the cinnamon sugar.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Apple Butter
recipes.coverPrompt: Jars of deep brown spiced apple butter with a spoon, some spread on toast, cinnamon sticks and apples nearby, warm light.
recipes.description: Deep, dark, spiced apple butter that makes the whole house smell like an orchard. Great on toast and in the oats.

steps.description: Peel, core and chop the apples. Add them to the slow cooker with the sugar, cider, spices and salt.
Cook on low, stirring every couple of hours, until the apples are very soft and dark.
Blend until smooth, then cook uncovered on high until thick enough to hold a line when you drag a spoon through it.
Stir in the vanilla and spoon into clean jars. Keeps in the fridge for three weeks.

recipes.title: Cupertino Breakfast Oats
recipes.coverPrompt: Overnight oats in a glass jar topped with grated apple, cinnamon and a swirl of apple butter, clean desk-side morning light.
recipes.description: Overnight oats with grated apple, cinnamon and a spoon of apple butter. Ready before your first meeting.

steps.description: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, cinnamon and maple syrup together in a jar.
Grate the apple straight into the jar, skin and all, and stir it through.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least four hours.
Loosen with a splash of milk, then top with apple butter and toasted pecans.

forks.title: Brown Butter Apple Crumble, with pecans
forks.coverPrompt: Brown butter apple crumble scattered with toasted pecans, a scoop of vanilla ice cream melting on top, served from the dish.

cooks.note: Made two for the offsite. Gone before the keynote even started.
Used a Normandy cider. Unreal sauce.
Flipped it in one go. Caramel was perfect at deep amber.
